resolutions: Integrated antecessive placement is a genuine carrier choice only for a preposed shared subject or object supplement before an antecessive VNC; elsewhere it is unavailable.
A short personal-pronominal NNC remains a complete clause but cannot become an independent utterance; composition status, not its English pronoun translation, controls the boundary.
Licensed cāti spelling variants are projections and never identify which graphically similar pronominal construction the user supplied.
Adjunctor in subordinates the complete following clause or sentence and does not determine an NNC predicate's number or definiteness.
Marked supplementation preserves the typed subject, object, possessor, topic, and recursive roles already present in the composition.
Traditional demonstrative fusion is a written projection of typed in plus a demonstrative NNC and cannot authorize the grammatical relation from a fused string.
Discontinuous supplementation is derived from a selected order containing an owner-issued intervening clause; it is not an independent construction toggle.
Distance and topic movement do not break a typed supplement-head reference edge or any larger recursive supplementation hierarchy.
Collective agreement is licensed only from typed plural reference; a visible singular form cannot create the exception by itself.
The unresolved moch formula analysis remains a reading or projection issue and is not collapsed into a single invented analysis.
Named-partner agreement is derived from a typed plural group containing a known speaker or addressee plus the captured third-person partner.
Named-partner status is never a user-facing exception switch and cannot be inferred from a surface string.
Male-bonding cross-reference requires an owner-issued male speaker who belongs to the referenced group; women and nonmembers are blocked from that route.
Oquich-tli alone cannot license first-person-plural cross-reference, and the ordinary third-person alternative remains available.
A specific patient of āyi automatically receives a silent 0-0 nuclear object head, while a nonspecific patient follows the overt tla route.
The silent-object route is restricted to typed āyi with its canonical āx perfective relation and cannot be transferred to ichtequi.
Ca-h deletion is derived only when a typed adverbial modifier and supplementary NNC subject share that principal; deletion kind is not a free user switch.
Deleting ca-h promotes its adverbial modifier to proxy principal and its former supplementary subject to surface subject without erasing the recoverable grammatical head.
A second-person NNC supplement of an optative VNC is a command subject rather than a real vocative, regardless of an address-like English translation.
A real vocative requires a typed third-person NNC plus owner-issued speaker sex; male e and female high-tone realization are automatic consequences.
Supportive-i absorption is automatic, while glottal-y and silent plural-in appear as choices only when the typed source licenses both surfaces.
Free order changes linear placement but never silently changes principal selection, supplement role, or referent identity.
Repeated and recursively nested supplements retain an acyclic typed clause graph and cannot be reconstructed from distance, markers, or translation strings.
NNCs such as chichi and nehhuātl remain complete clauses inside a larger composition even when their English translations look like isolated words.
